title: An Artificial Prefrontal Cortex for LLM Agents: A Structural Executive Module That Intercepts Jailbreaks, Collusion, Mutation Attempts and Long Horizon Evasion Tactics
content: Current attempts to instill internal alignment mechanisms into modern AI systems remain brittle when applied to autonomous, tool using agents facing out of distribution adversarial attacks, multi-step evasion strategies, and context smuggling. To date, none of the attempts at instilling internal alignment safety protocols have computationally modeled the approach developed by evolution to guide humans away from rogue behaviors and towards socially aligned ones. In human neurobiology, behavioral safety is enforced through hierarchical, intrinsic executive inhibition mediated by the prefrontal cortex (PFC). When PFC function is impaired by disease, trauma, or developmental conditions, disinhibition, poor judgment, and rule-violating behaviors emerge. Drawing on this biomimetic principle, we propose and prototype a structural containment framework-the Artificial Prefrontal Cortex (aPFC)-that provides an external layer of executive control over LLM based autonomous agents. Using Gemma 4-e4b and a Python based implementation, this pa- per presents a prototypical executive control architecture that remained robust under diverse adversarial conditions, including authority framing jailbreaks, multi node collusion, stealth payload mutation, context smug- gling, buffer flushing, and long horizon evasion. The architecture intro- duces a decoupled Executive Control module composed of four functional analogues inspired by human PFC organization: (1) a deterministic reflex layer providing zero latency constraint enforcement for known vulnera- bilities; (2) a coordination and perseveration detector that terminates unauthorized multi agent swarming and repeated evasion loops; (3) a se- mantic working memory evaluator that uses an LLM to assess the intent and consequences of proposed actions; and (4) an event driven temporal tracker that consolidates multi step behaviors to mitigate buffer flushing and “temporal amnesia” attacks.  Empirical validation in an air-gapped simulation environment demon- strated that the system autonomously intercepted authority framing jail- breaks, multi node collusion, stealth payload mutations, and long horizon evasion tactics. These findings suggest that securing autonomous AI sys- tems requires moving beyond current internal model alignment and toward structural executive containment, providing a scalable and model agnostic blueprint for next generation AI safety.
